research_mode: official Home Office 2026 technical annex only; validation, HODH, Crimsec4 and cross-force comparison boundaries; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Monthly crime outcome and cancellation supply
verified_claims: the Home Office receives monthly crime and outcome data from forces
monthly supply also covers transferred or cancelled records
fraud and Computer Misuse Act offences are excluded from this collection
limitations: monthly supply scope differs from national fraud collections
submission frequency does not ensure immediate publication

sources.name: Anomaly reports returned to forces
verified_claims: Home Office statisticians quality assure and analyse monthly data
identified anomalies or errors are reported back to the relevant force
forces validate or correct the affected data
limitations: the process does not prove all errors are detected
an anomaly query is not itself a confirmed error

sources.name: Pre-publication force verification exercise
verified_claims: a verification exercise is performed with all forces before publication
Home Office-held data are returned to each force for confirmation
forces can identify inconsistencies and resubmit data
limitations: force confirmation is one quality-control layer rather than independent audit
post-verification revisions can still occur

sources.name: HODH record-level detail
verified_claims: the Home Office Data Hub accepts record-level offence detail
record-level supply expands analytical opportunities
HODH supports linked offence and outcome analysis
limitations: record-level availability does not guarantee public record-level release
source-system quality remains relevant

sources.name: HODH and remaining Crimsec4 coverage
verified_claims: 43 forces supplied monthly crime outcomes and transfer/cancellation data solely through HODH at publication
one remaining force supplied Crimsec4 returns
the Home Office was working toward full HODH operation
limitations: the coverage statement is edition-specific
HODH and Crimsec4 records have different granularity

sources.name: Crimsec4 monthly aggregate return
verified_claims: Crimsec4 is an aggregated monthly return
it collects recorded crime outcomes and transferred/cancelled records
collection is structured by notifiable offence classification
limitations: aggregates cannot reproduce all HODH record-level analysis
Crimsec4 and HODH outputs need source-mode metadata

sources.name: Crimsec4 outcome-month semantics
verified_claims: Crimsec4 records an outcome in the month it is applied
the original offence may have occurred or been recorded months earlier
outcome-month data do not correspond directly to offences recorded in the same month or year
limitations: monthly Crimsec4 outcomes must not be treated as same-month offence cohorts
lag analysis requires linked or additional returns

sources.name: New outcomes absent from Crimsec4 form
verified_claims: outcomes 20 21 and 22 are not included on Crimsec4 forms
the five transfer/cancellation subcategories are also absent
these items are collected through an additional quarterly manual return
limitations: Crimsec4 alone is incomplete for the current framework
monthly and quarterly inputs require reconciliation

sources.name: Remaining-force annual submission timing
verified_claims: year-ending-March HODH data are usually taken in early June
the remaining manual-return force supplies annual data on a different date
voluntary submission timing can range from early April to mid-June
limitations: cut-off timing differs by source mode
publication snapshots can contain differently matured inputs

sources.name: Force outcome-mix comparison caution
verified_claims: outcome comparisons between forces can be misleading
forces use outcomes differently and face different crime mixes
community resolutions and drug-offence prevalence are given as examples
limitations: raw outcome shares must not be ranked without case-mix adjustment
force-level differences are not parcel-level safety differences
